signature.name: Half-Awake Read Time
signature.description: Whether a tired, low-vision user can name 'coffee in progress' from one frozen frame at 120px, through grayscale and a 1.5x blur, with a deliberate reduced-motion cue and a specific accessible name.

lesson: Strong loaders keep a coffee subject and a progress cue visible in every frozen frame and under blur, and say so in a specific accessible name; weak ones only work while you watch them move.

bare-wire.signature_why: Frozen frames at 1.6s and 4.6s are a bare cup with no cue, the reduced pose is a dim ambiguous blob, and aria-label is only 'Loading'.
bare-wire.loved: Honest pitch, lean fills-only build, and the slow close of the hole is calm with a clean seam.
bare-wire.docked: At 120px roughly half of all frames (hole shrunk to a pin-dot) show no progress cue at all, so the loader reads as a static cup to a half-awake glance.
bare-wire.fix_note: Five travelling scars were refused as spinner grammar and clutter, which is a fair reason, but the 75ms fade-in is far short of my 0.4s and the dead-frame problem remains.

warm-hands.signature_why: Top-down coffee, a held pour stream and spiral survive grayscale and blur with strong contrast, the reduced pose keeps the stream, and the label 'your coffee is being made' is specific.
warm-hands.loved: The stream now visibly feeds the spiral, so the frozen frame says someone is pouring, and the reduced-motion pose keeps that cue.
warm-hands.docked: The spiral is still the biggest turning shape and thin rim-stain strokes turn to mush under blur, so spinner or cinnamon-roll can still win in a 2-second glance.
warm-hands.fix_note: Stream added from rim to spiral origin and held in reduced motion, stroke 6.5 instead of 7 with a sound reason; verified in code and frames.

the-glitch.signature_why: Light cup on dark, spout and falling drop read as coffee even in blurred grayscale, the crema steps are a real progress cue, and the aria-label names the order; early dark crema steps are low contrast.
the-glitch.loved: The slip and orange ghost are gone and nothing cuts, leaving a calm countable one-drop-per-second rhythm that honestly names its fill-and-reset risk.
the-glitch.docked: The fifth crema step peaks near full and then snaps back in 0.25s, which can read as fill-then-drain, and the early crema steps are faint against the dark coffee.
the-glitch.fix_note: Slip, ghost and hard cuts all deleted and the drop now fades in and squash-fades out; code matches the pitch.
